Data centre white space · drawings & 3D

I draw the inside of data centres.

General arrangement plans, floor plans, rack layouts and 3D visuals of white space — for teams that are out of drafting capacity.

Who is doing the drawing

Colleen Chiu. I came to this from the controls side — building and environmental control systems on live sites, where the job is to represent a real room accurately enough that an operator can act on it. I now work both ends: the 3D model of the space, and the graphic the operators watch it on.

Everything is modelled in SketchUp and rendered in V-Ray. Drawings come out of the same model, so the plan and the visual never disagree.

Equipment is modelled, not blocked in. Patch panels, breaker faces, rack rails, door hardware — the things that let someone recognise their own kit in a picture of a room that does not exist yet.

Study 01

Colocation hall, caged suites

30.0 × 18.0 m · 10 cages + 2 private suites + MMR · 116 rack positions

Subdividing white space is a commercial problem before it is a technical one: the drawing has to answer who can walk where. Wire mesh, solid partition and aisle containment are three different things at three different heights, and only one of them is a wall.

Study 02

Air-cooled data hall

Cold aisle containment · perimeter CRAC · 600 mm raised floor

One open hall, three containment pods. The plan, the axonometric and the rendered views all come out of the same model — which is not always true of the drawing sets I am asked to work from.

Send me a marked-up PDF of a room and I'll come back with a scope and a price.

No brief needed. A sketch, a survey drawing, or a photograph of a whiteboard is enough to start from.

Working together

I work from
Your layouts, sketches, point lists, or a written spec. Marked-up PDFs are fine.
Stays with you
The engineering. I draw what your engineers have decided; I don't specify it.
Deliverables
Rendered stills at 3000 px or larger, general arrangement plans, axonometrics, section views, operator-screen backgrounds. Source files on request.
File formats
PNG, PDF, DWG / DXF, SKP, OBJ / FBX.
Typical turnaround
Depends on scope. A single general arrangement plan with one rendered view is usually a few days. A full set with sections and multiple views takes longer. You get a date with the quote, before anything starts.
Pricing
Quoted per job against your brief, not by the hour. Fixed figure agreed before I start, revisions to the agreed scope included.
Confidentiality
Client work is covered by NDA and is not shown here. I'm happy to sign yours before you send anything.
Where I am
Remote, Taiwan, GMT+8. Work generally goes out overnight from Europe and the US.
